rows.name: NUM_USERS
rows.values: Integer count of requests. The script uses the text in bash arithmetic. The script does not validate it.
rows.effect: `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a local server) sends this number of requests. Each request starts at a random time inside the arrival window that `WINDOW_MS` sets.
rows.notes: The option `-n` or `--num-users` overrides the variable.

rows.name: PAIRING
rows.values: `random` or `cycle`, as exact text. Any other text stops the script with exit status 1.
rows.effect: `random` draws the system prompt and the user question at random for each request of `burst-test.sh`. `cycle` walks the 256 pairs of 16 system prompts and 16 user questions in a fixed order.
rows.notes: The option `-c` or `--cycle-prompts` sets `cycle` and overrides the variable. The script sends the user question only when `PROMPT_MODE` is `short`.

rows.name: PERFETTO_BIN_DIR
rows.who_sets: The Nix apps `tronperf` and `wrapper`, two CI workflows, or a developer.
rows.values: Path of a directory. `tronperf` and `wrapper` need executable files `perfetto`, `traced` and `traced_probes` in it. `perfetto_capture.py` needs the files `traced` and `perfetto`.
rows.default: Unset: `tronperf` and `wrapper` use `PERFETTO_HOME`. The Nix apps use the Nix package `perfetto-host-binaries`. `resolve-perfetto-bin-dir.sh` builds that package. `perfetto_capture.py` raises an error.
rows.effect: `tronperf` and `wrapper` (the Perfetto capture scripts in `perfetto/`) start `perfetto`, `traced` and `traced_probes` from this directory. `bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py` starts `traced` and `perfetto` from it. `bin/ci/resolve-perfetto-bin-dir.sh` prints a non-empty value unchanged and runs no build.
rows.notes: It takes priority over `PERFETTO_HOME`. In `perfetto_capture.py` the option `--bin-dir` takes priority over it. A missing program stops `tronperf` and `wrapper` with exit status 2. The Nix apps are `nix run .#tronperf` and `nix run .#wrapper`. `bin/ci/test-perfetto-capture.sh` also reads it.

rows.name: PERFETTO_HOME
rows.who_sets: A developer who uses a custom Perfetto build.
rows.values: Path of a directory. The scripts use its sub-directory `out/linux`. That sub-directory must hold executable files `perfetto`, `traced` and `traced_probes`.
rows.default: Unset: no effect. When `PERFETTO_BIN_DIR` is also unset or empty, `tronperf` and `wrapper` print an error and exit with status 2.
rows.effect: `tronperf` and `wrapper` (the Perfetto capture scripts in `perfetto/`) start `perfetto`, `traced` and `traced_probes` from `$PERFETTO_HOME/out/linux`. The scripts use `PERFETTO_HOME` only when `PERFETTO_BIN_DIR` is unset or empty.
rows.notes: `nix run .#tronperf` and `nix run .#wrapper` always export a non-empty `PERFETTO_BIN_DIR`. `PERFETTO_HOME` then has no effect. A missing program stops the script with exit status 2.

evidence.quote: echo "error: Perfetto binaries are not configured." >&2

rows.name: PERFETTO_RESOLVE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
rows.who_sets: No workflow sets it. `bin/ci/test-perfetto-capture.sh` sets it for two checks.
rows.values: Number of seconds. The script passes the text unchanged to the `timeout` command as the time limit. The script does not check the text.
rows.effect: It limits the run time of `nix build .#perfetto-host-binaries` in `resolve-perfetto-bin-dir.sh` (the script that prints the Perfetto program directory). At the limit, `timeout` sends TERM, and KILL 30 seconds later if the build still runs. The script then prints a hint and exits with status 124 or 137.
rows.notes: The script does not read it when `PERFETTO_BIN_DIR` is non-empty. When `nix build` fails before the limit, the script exits with the status of `nix build`.

rows.name: PLUGIN_DIR
rows.who_sets: A developer. `config/test_model_definitions.py` sets it for one test.
rows.values: Path of a directory. The script does not check it.
rows.default: Unset: the directory `gen/src/tron/h/tron/plugins` of the checkout.
rows.effect: `ingest/build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for every ingest model of `config/models.yaml`) passes the path to `ingest/build-model.py` as `--plugin-dir`. `build-model.py` passes it to the ingest program as the output directory of the generated model plugin.
rows.notes: The CMake variable `PLUGIN_DIR` in `ingest/CMakeLists.txt` is a separate variable. It is not an environment variable.

evidence.quote: help="Directory in which to place produced model plugin (created if necessary)",

rows.name: PROMPT_MODE
rows.values: `long` or `short`, as exact text. Any other text stops the script with exit status 1.
rows.effect: `long` makes `burst-test.sh` send an English passage and ask the model to repeat it. The passage size is drawn at random between `PROMPT_TOKENS_MIN` and `PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX`. `short` sends one of 16 short questions.
rows.notes: The option `-s` or `--short-prompts` sets `short` and overrides the variable.

rows.name: PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX
rows.values: Integer number of estimated tokens. It must not be smaller than `PROMPT_TOKENS_MIN`. Otherwise the script exits with status 1.
rows.effect: It is the upper limit of the prompt size that each request of `burst-test.sh` draws at random when `PROMPT_MODE` is `long`. The script header says that the context window of the model must cover `PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX` plus `MAX_TOKENS_BASE` plus `MAX_TOKENS_JITTER`.
rows.notes: The script counts 3 words as 4 tokens. It builds the passage from whole paragraphs. The passage can be larger than the drawn size. The option `-P` or `--prompt-max` overrides the variable.

rows.name: PROMPT_TOKENS_MIN
rows.values: Integer number of estimated tokens. It must be at least 1 and not larger than `PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX`. Otherwise the script exits with status 1.
rows.effect: It is the lower limit of the prompt size when `PROMPT_MODE` is `long`. Each request of `burst-test.sh` draws its size at random between `PROMPT_TOKENS_MIN` and `PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX`.
rows.notes: The script counts 3 words as 4 tokens. The range check also runs when `PROMPT_MODE` is `short`. The option `-p` or `--prompt-min` overrides the variable.

rows.name: RUN_COVERAGE
rows.who_sets: A developer. No file in the checkout sets it.
rows.values: List of Hugging Face model IDs, separated by white space. The script compares each ID with the model ID from `config/models.yaml` as exact text.
rows.effect: When `COVERAGE` is non-empty, `ingest/build-all.sh` exports only the models in this list. It skips every other model and prints a message.
rows.notes: The script ignores it when `COVERAGE` is unset or empty. The target `build-all-coverage` of `ingest/Makefile` sets `COVERAGE=1` and does not set `RUN_COVERAGE`.

rows.name: RZ_CLI_ARGS
rows.who_sets: Not set in the checkout. The unit loads it from environment files.
rows.read_by: Nothing in TRON. systemd expands it in the `ExecStart` line of the unit `rinzler@.service` (`packaging/systemd/rinzler@.service`, `packaging/tron-host/90-rinzler-host.conf`).
rows.values: Command-line arguments of `rinzler`. The unit uses the form `$RZ_CLI_ARGS` without braces. systemd splits that form at white space into separate arguments.
rows.default: Unset: the unit and the drop-in give no fallback value. No file in the checkout sets the variable.
rows.effect: systemd puts the arguments after `/opt/positron/bin/rinzler` on the `ExecStart` line of the unit `rinzler@.service`. With the drop-in `90-rinzler-host.conf`, the program is `rinzler_host` (the CPU inference build for test and development hosts), and `--host 127.0.0.1` follows the arguments.
rows.notes: The unit loads `/etc/rinzler/instance-<name>.env` and the optional `/opt/positron/user/config.env`. `<name>` is the systemd instance name of the unit. The unit comment says that platformd writes the first file. `packaging/tron-host/README` says that platformd passes `--model-path`, `--app-cores`, `--dev-cores` and `--numa`.

rows.name: SEED
rows.values: Integer. The script assigns the text to the bash variable `RANDOM`. The script does not check the text.
rows.default: Unset: the script does not seed `RANDOM`.
rows.effect: `burst-test.sh` assigns a non-empty value to the bash variable `RANDOM` before the first random draw. The draws of arrival offsets, `max_tokens` values, prompt sizes and prompt pairs then come from the seeded generator. The script comment says that a fixed value reproduces the schedule.
rows.notes: The option `-S` or `--seed` overrides the variable.

evidence.quote: # Draw all randomness in the parent shell so a fixed SEED reproduces the

rows.name: STREAMING
rows.values: `true` or `false`. The script compares the text with `true`. It also passes the text to `jq` as the JSON value of the request field `stream`.
rows.effect: `true` makes `burst-test.sh` send streaming requests. The script then checks that each stream ends with `[DONE]` and holds no error frame. `false` sends blocking requests.
rows.notes: The option `-b` or `--blocking` sets `false` and overrides the variable. Text that is not valid JSON, for example `yes`, makes `jq` fail. The request then counts as failed. Other JSON, for example `1`, is sent as written and handled as a blocking request.

rows.name: TRACE_DEST_IP
rows.who_sets: A developer who wants the trace on another host.
rows.values: Host name or address of an `scp` destination. `tronperf` adds `:` after the text. `tronperf` does not check the text.
rows.default: Unset: `tronperf` does not copy the trace.
rows.effect: After a capture without errors, `tronperf` (the script that captures a Perfetto trace of one runtron run) copies the trace file to that host with `scp -C`. The file goes to the home directory of the remote user.
rows.notes: `tronperf` skips the copy when runtron, the `perfetto` client or a Perfetto daemon ends with an error. When `scp` fails, `tronperf` exits with the `scp` status. `perfetto/wrapper` does not read the variable.

rows.name: TRON_BENCHMARK_DIR
rows.values: Path of a directory. The scripts do not check it.
rows.default: Unset: `/scratch/tron-benchmark`. Empty: `benchmark_save.py` uses the empty text, and the result file path starts at the root directory `/`.
rows.effect: `bin/ci/benchmark_save.py` (the script that runs benchmarks and saves the samples) reads and writes its result file in this directory. The file name is `<commit>.<host name>.json`, with the first 7 characters of the commit. The script loads an existing file and skips configurations that already have enough samples.
rows.notes: `run_benchmark.sh` exports it with the value of `TRON_BENCHMARK_RESULTS_ROOT`. `benchmark-golden.yml` sets `/scratch/tron-benchmark-golden`. `bin/ci/benchmark_info.py` does not read it. The function `golden_trace_dir` in `bin/ci/benchmark_lib.py` treats an empty value as unset.

rows.name: TRON_BENCHMARK_TRACE_DIR
rows.who_sets: Nothing in the checkout sets it.
rows.read_by: The function `golden_trace_dir` (`bin/ci/benchmark_lib.py`). No code in the checkout calls this function.
rows.values: Path of a directory. The function returns a non-empty value unchanged.
rows.default: Unset: `<TRON_BENCHMARK_DIR>/traces`. When `TRON_BENCHMARK_DIR` is also unset or empty, the value is `/scratch/tron-benchmark/traces`.
rows.effect: The function `golden_trace_dir` returns the value as the root directory for Perfetto traces of the golden benchmark (the nightly benchmark of the workflow `benchmark-golden.yml`). The function comment gives the layout `<host>/<sha7>/<workload-slug>/<repeat>.perfetto-trace` below it.
rows.notes: No code in the checkout calls `golden_trace_dir`. No checked-in program reads the variable at run time. An empty value counts as unset.

rows.name: TRON_INGEST_LIBSTDCXX_PATH
rows.who_sets: The Nix dev shell and the derivation in `nix/model-traces.nix`.
rows.values: Path of the directory that holds `libstdc++`. The script does not check the text.
rows.default: Unset: `build-model.py` does not change `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` of the export subprocess.
rows.effect: `ingest/build-model.py` puts the directory at the front of `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for its export subprocess (the ingest step that exports the PyTorch model trace). Later subprocesses of the script do not get the change.
rows.notes: The script reads it only when the export step runs. The option `--skip-export` skips that step. Nix sets it to the `libstdc++` directory of the Nix compiler on Linux, and to an empty string on other systems.

evidence.quote: env["LD_LIBRARY_PATH"] = f"{libstdcxx}:{existing}" if existing else libstdcxx

new_terms.definition: The load script `perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh`. It sends a burst of chat completion requests to a local server, for Perfetto capture under load.
The prompt size unit of `burst-test.sh`. The script counts 3 words as 4 tokens.
The script `perfetto/tronperf`. It starts the Perfetto programs, runs runtron once and captures a trace.
The script `perfetto/wrapper`. It starts the Perfetto programs and captures a trace of a running process, for example rinzler.
A program that `nix run .#<name>` starts. `flake.nix` defines the Nix apps `tronperf` and `wrapper` for x86_64 Linux.
The Nix package in `flake.nix` that holds the Perfetto programs `perfetto`, `traced` and `traced_probes`.
The capture harness `bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py`. It starts its own `traced` and `perfetto` around one command and writes a trace file.
The script `bin/ci/resolve-perfetto-bin-dir.sh`. It prints a directory that holds the Perfetto programs. It builds the Nix package `perfetto-host-binaries` when `PERFETTO_BIN_DIR` is unset.
The script `ingest/build-all.sh`. It runs `ingest/build-model.py` for every ingest model of the model registry `config/models.yaml`.
The script `ingest/build-model.py`. It exports the trace of one PyTorch model and then runs the ingest program on the trace.
The first step of `ingest/build-model.py`. A subprocess runs `ingest/export/torch_export.py` and writes the model trace.
A build of rinzler that runs inference on the CPU. The package `tron-host` installs it. It is for test and development hosts only.
A systemd file that changes settings of an installed unit. `packaging/tron-host/90-rinzler-host.conf` is a drop-in for `rinzler@.service`.
The nightly benchmark of the workflow `.github/workflows/benchmark-golden.yml`. It runs `bin/ci/benchmark_save.py --golden`.

notes: PERFETTO_BIN_DIR has 4 readers with 4 different unset behaviours. The cross-area finding asks for one row per reader. This chunk keeps one row and names each reader in the cells. The behaviour of `bin/ci/test-perfetto-capture.sh` is not described in that row. That script runs its integration checks only when the directory holds executable `traced` and `perfetto`. RZ_CLI_ARGS is a variable of the packaged systemd unit, not of a developer tool. It fits a deployment or packaging section better than the tools section. Its `values` cell states the systemd rule for the form `$NAME` without braces. That rule comes from systemd.service(5), not from the checkout. The checkout does not state which file sets RZ_CLI_ARGS. TRON_BENCHMARK_TRACE_DIR is read only by the function `golden_trace_dir`, and no code in the checkout calls that function. TRACE_DEST_IP: the statement that the file goes to the remote home directory comes from the `scp` rule for a destination that ends with `:`. SEED: the list of seeded draws leaves out the start paragraph and the run ID of each run. Both also come from `RANDOM`.
